# CLI Reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm docs:reference` from the command schema. Do not edit by hand. -->

## Global Options

| Flag | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | boolean | Print the result as JSON, even on a terminal. |

## Envelope

With `--json`, or whenever stdout is piped, stdout carries exactly one JSON value. A success is `{"data": ...}`. A failure is `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "details": ...}}`, where `details` is omitted when empty. Each command below shows its `data`. On a terminal without `--json`, a command prints a table or text, and a failure prints `jm: <message>` to stderr. `--help` and `--version` always print plain text.

## Exit Codes

| Exit | Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Success |
| 2 | `validation_failed` | A flag, argument or value is missing, unknown or invalid, or Jira rejected the input. |
| 3 | `not_found` | The issue, comment, worklog, link, attachment, sprint, view or timer does not exist. |
| 4 | `permission_denied` | Jira refused the credentials, or no one is logged in. |
| 5 | `jira_error` | Jira failed or sent a response the CLI cannot read, after the CLI retried. |
| 1 | `internal` | A bug in jm. |
| 130 |  | Interrupted with Ctrl-C |

Every error code, with its fix, is in [errors.md](errors.md).

## auth

### jm auth login

```
jm auth login [--site <url>] [--project <key>] [--email <text>] [--token-stdin]
```

Verifies the credentials against Jira, saves the site, project and email to the settings file and the token to the Keychain. On a terminal it prompts for a missing site, project, email or token. The token never travels in a flag.

#### Options

| Flag | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--site <url>` | text | no |  | The Jira site URL. Defaults to the settings file. |
| `--project <key>` | text | no |  | The Jira project key. Defaults to the settings file. |
| `--email <text>` | text | no |  | The account email. Defaults to the settings file. |
| `--token-stdin` | boolean | no |  | Read the API token from stdin. |

#### Examples

```sh
# Log in, prompting for what is missing.
jm auth login
```

```sh
# Log in without prompts, reading the token from stdin.
jm auth login --site https://example.atlassian.net --project PSAPAC --email me@example.com --token-stdin
```

#### Output

The account that is now logged in.

```json
{
  "data": {
    "siteUrl": "https://example.atlassian.net",
    "projectKey": "PSAPAC",
    "email": "me@example.com",
    "accountId": "5b10ac8d82e05b22cc7d4ef5",
    "displayName": "Shane Dolley"
  }
}
```

#### Exits

| Exit | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | `validation_failed` | A value is missing and there is no terminal to prompt on. |
| 4 | `permission_denied` | Jira refuses the token. |

#### Effects

Writes: state, keychain.

Calls:

- `@jira-mgr/core/auth#login`

### jm auth status

```
jm auth status
```

Show who is logged in

#### Examples

```sh
# Show the logged-in account.
jm auth status
```

#### Output

The logged-in account and when the custom fields were last resolved.

```json
{
  "data": {
    "siteUrl": "https://example.atlassian.net",
    "projectKey": "PSAPAC",
    "email": "me@example.com",
    "accountId": "5b10ac8d82e05b22cc7d4ef5",
    "displayName": "Shane Dolley",
    "fieldsResolvedAt": "2026-10-06T23:10:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

#### Exits

| Exit | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | `permission_denied` | No one is logged in. |

#### Effects

Writes: nothing.

Calls:

- `@jira-mgr/core/auth#getCredentials`
- `@jira-mgr/core/state#readFields`
- `@jira-mgr/core/lookups#getCurrentUser`

### jm auth logout

```
jm auth logout
```

Remove the stored token

#### Examples

```sh
# Log out. Succeeds when already logged out.
jm auth logout
```

#### Output

Confirms the logout.

```json
{
  "data": {
    "loggedOut": true
  }
}
```

#### Effects

Writes: keychain, state.

Calls:

- `@jira-mgr/core/auth#logout`

## help

### jm help

```
jm help [command...]
```

Prints help for a command. With `--json`, or when piped, it prints the help document: every command with its flags, examples, output and exit codes. Name a command to print only that command.

#### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command...` | text | no | A command path, such as `issue delete`. |

#### Examples

```sh
# Print every command as JSON.
jm help --json
```

```sh
# Print one command as JSON.
jm help issue delete --json
```

#### Output

The help document, or one command object when a command is named.

```json
{
  "data": {
    "name": "jm",
    "version": "0.0.0",
    "globalOptions": [],
    "exitCodes": [],
    "commands": []
  }
}
```

#### Exits

| Exit | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | `validation_failed` | The named command does not exist. |

#### Effects

Writes: nothing.

Calls: none.
